Reflection, attributes and late binding

Inspect a type and call a member using information discovered while the program runs.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A shared toolbox and a console app that uses it

Put reusable rules in a class library, then call them from a console project. Explore how C# can inspect types or create a small type at runtime.

The example prints results in the console; it does not use a database.

Check the result

Build both projects together, run the console app and check the rule and reflection output.

Reflection lets a running program inspect a type’s description. It is like reading labels on a toolbox before choosing a tool.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Inspect and invoke

Type type = typeof(MarkRules);
var method = type.GetMethod(nameof(MarkRules.IsPass))!;
object? result = method.Invoke(null, new object[] { 40 });

Expected late-binding result: False. null is the target for a static method. Parameters must match the signature. For an instance method create/provide an instance. Check for a missing method instead of using null-forgiving syntax in general dynamic input code. Invocation errors can wrap the inner failure in TargetInvocationException.

Attributes are metadata

StudyTopicAttribute attaches a Title to MarkRules. AttributeUsage limits where it can appear. GetCustomAttribute reads it; an attribute does not execute a rule by magic. Reflection is useful for serializers, discovery, testing tools and plugin contracts, but ordinary direct calls are clearer and checked earlier. Trimming and Native AOT can require explicit metadata preservation; arbitrary reflection is not always deployment-friendly.

Try it yourself

What changes if IsPass becomes an instance method?

Worked answer

Create an instance and pass it as Invoke’s target instead of null.

How do you handle a user-supplied method name?

Worked answer

Avoid unrestricted invocation. Allowlist approved operations and validate arguments and access. Reflection is not an authorisation system.

Predict and practise

Can reflection discover methods while a program is running?

Check your prediction

Yes. It inspects type metadata and can invoke members when supplied suitable arguments.

Make one change

Locate GetType or typeof and inspect the discovered members.

Worked guidance

Compare the metadata name with the actual class or method declaration.

Try independently

Inspect your own small class and print its public property names.
